questions.text:
Let [latex] f(x) [/latex] be a continuous function from [latex] \mathbb{R} [/latex] to [latex] \mathbb{R} [/latex] such that
[latex] f(x)=1-f(2-x) [/latex]
Which one of the following options is the CORRECT value of [latex] \int_0^2 f(x) d x [/latex] ?
questions.solution:
Let [latex]I=\int_0^2 f(x)\,dx[/latex]. Substituting [latex]x\to2-x[/latex] gives [latex]I=\int_0^2 f(2-x)\,dx[/latex].

Adding both: [latex]2I=\int_0^2\big(f(x)+f(2-x)\big)dx=\int_0^2 1\,dx=2[/latex]

[latex]I=1[/latex]

Answer: 1

questions.text: Let [latex] A  [/latex] be the adjacency matrix of a simple undirected graph [latex]G[/latex]. Suppose [latex]A[/latex] is its own inverse. Which one of the following statements is always TRUE?
questions.solution:
[latex]A=A^{-1}\Rightarrow A^2=I[/latex].

- [latex](A^2)_{ii}[/latex] = degree of vertex [latex]i[/latex] = 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] every vertex has exactly one neighbour.
- [latex](A^2)_{ij}=0[/latex] for [latex]i\ne j[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] consistent with that.

A graph where every vertex has degree exactly 1 is a set of disjoint edges covering all vertices [latex]\text{---}[/latex] a perfect matching.

Answer: G is a perfect matching

questions.text:
When six unbiased dice are rolled simultaneously, the probability of getting all
distinct numbers (i.e., 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6) is
questions.solution:
Total outcomes [latex]=6^6=46656[/latex].
All distinct means the six dice show 1-6 in some order: [latex]6!=720[/latex] outcomes.

[latex]P=\dfrac{720}{46656}=\dfrac{5}{324}[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\frac{5}{324}[/latex]

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text:
Once the DBMS informs the user that a transaction has been successfully
completed, its effect should persist even if the system crashes before all its changes
are reflected on disk. This property is called
questions.solution:
Once a transaction commits, its changes must survive any later crash (using the log for recovery). This is the Durability property of ACID.

Answer: durability

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text: In the context of owner and weak entity sets in the ER (Entity-Relationship) data model, which one of the following statements is TRUE?
questions.solution:
A weak entity cannot exist without its owner, so every weak entity must take part in the identifying relationship [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] total participation of the weak entity set.

An owner may have no weak entities (e.g. an employee with no dependents), so the owner's participation is not necessarily total.

Answer: The weak entity set MUST have total participation in the identifying relationship

options: The weak entity set MUST have total participation in the identifying relationship
The owner entity set MUST have total participation in the identifying relationship
Both weak and owner entity sets MUST have total participation in the identifying relationship
Neither weak entity set nor owner entity set MUST have total participation in the identifying relationship
